metadata.description: CPSS practice scenarios for pilot aptitude assessment

scenarios.scenario: Your aircraft's attitude indicator shows a 15° bank to the left, but the turn coordinator indicates wings level. Determine which instrument has failed and take corrective action.
scenarios.context: Day VFR flight at FL150. Smooth air conditions. Last instrument check was 30 minutes ago.

scenarios.scenario: During a night reconnaissance mission, you discover an unidentified vessel in restricted waters. It is not responding to radio calls and appears to be heading towards a strategic naval installation.
scenarios.context: Maritime patrol aircraft at 1000 feet. Naval HQ is 200nm away. No naval vessels in immediate vicinity. Moon illumination is 40%.
constraints: Cannot descend below 500 feet due to mast height uncertainty
Radio relay is required for HQ contact
Fuel remaining for 2 hours on station

scenarios.scenario: You detect a hostile surface-to-air missile launch against your formation. Execute defensive maneuvers while coordinating your flight to suppress the missile site.
scenarios.context: Hostile territory penetration mission. SAM site was not in the intelligence briefing. Your formation is a 4-ship at low level.

scenarios.scenario: Track a target on radar that is maneuvering erratically at close range while maintaining your own aircraft in a defensive orbit pattern.
scenarios.context: Air combat training exercise. Target is a MiG-29 equivalent performing high-G maneuvers. You are in a Su-30MKI.

scenarios.scenario: During a combat air patrol, your radar detects an unknown aircraft approaching the air defense identification zone at high speed. You have 4 minutes to intercept and identify before it enters national airspace.
scenarios.context: Alert scramble during peacetime. ROE requires visual identification before any engagement. The bogey is at FL400, Mach 1.2.
constraints: Fuel state allows one intercept attempt
Bogey is not responding to IFF

scenarios.scenario: Brief a 4-aircraft formation for a dawn raid on an enemy airfield that has both fixed-wing and helicopter assets. Intelligence shows 2 SAM sites defending the base.
scenarios.context: Pre-planned strike mission. Airfield has hardened shelters and dispersed parking. Time on target is 0530 hours. Weather forecast is clear.
constraints: One aircraft has reduced weapons load

scenarios.scenario: Your altimeter setting is in hectopascals but the approach plate shows altitude in feet with QNH in inches of mercury. Convert and set the correct pressure.
scenarios.context: International flight arriving at a foreign military base. Night approach with published minima of 300 feet AGL.

scenarios.scenario: While landing in a crosswind of 25 knots gusting to 35, your aircraft touches down off-center on the runway. The aircraft begins to drift towards the runway edge.
scenarios.context: Wet runway surface. Fighter aircraft with narrow track landing gear. No arresting barrier available. Wind from the left.
constraints: Following aircraft is on short final

scenarios.scenario: Plan a night helicopter insertion of special forces into a target compound located in an urban area with significant civilian population.
scenarios.context: Counter-terrorism operation. Intelligence confirms 5 hostiles in a 3-story building. 12 special forces operators to be inserted. Two helicopter available.
objectives: Select landing zones close to target
constraints: Dogs in the area will alert

scenarios.scenario: While flying a helicopter in a mountain valley, sudden wind shear forces a rapid attitude change. Recover the aircraft and navigate out of the valley safely.
scenarios.context: Casualty evacuation mission. Patient on board requires urgent care. Valley is 500m wide with 2000m peaks on either side.

scenarios.scenario: While flying a helicopter in a mountain valley, sudden wind shear forces a rapid attitude change. Recover the aircraft and navigate out of the valley safely.
scenarios.context: Casualty evacuation mission. Patient on board requires urgent care. Valley is 500m wide with 2000m peaks on either side.

scenarios.scenario: Your aircraft's attitude indicator shows a 15° bank to the left, but the turn coordinator indicates wings level. Determine which instrument has failed and take corrective action.
scenarios.context: Day VFR flight at FL150. Smooth air conditions. Last instrument check was 30 minutes ago.

scenarios.scenario: During a night reconnaissance mission, you discover an unidentified vessel in restricted waters. It is not responding to radio calls and appears to be heading towards a strategic naval installation.
scenarios.context: Maritime patrol aircraft at 1000 feet. Naval HQ is 200nm away. No naval vessels in immediate vicinity. Moon illumination is 40%.
constraints: Cannot descend below 500 feet due to mast height uncertainty
Radio relay is required for HQ contact
Fuel remaining for 2 hours on station

scenarios.scenario: You detect a hostile surface-to-air missile launch against your formation. Execute defensive maneuvers while coordinating your flight to suppress the missile site.
scenarios.context: Hostile territory penetration mission. SAM site was not in the intelligence briefing. Your formation is a 4-ship at low level.

scenarios.scenario: Track a target on radar that is maneuvering erratically at close range while maintaining your own aircraft in a defensive orbit pattern.
scenarios.context: Air combat training exercise. Target is a MiG-29 equivalent performing high-G maneuvers. You are in a Su-30MKI.

scenarios.scenario: During a combat air patrol, your radar detects an unknown aircraft approaching the air defense identification zone at high speed. You have 4 minutes to intercept and identify before it enters national airspace.
scenarios.context: Alert scramble during peacetime. ROE requires visual identification before any engagement. The bogey is at FL400, Mach 1.2.
constraints: Fuel state allows one intercept attempt
Bogey is not responding to IFF

scenarios.scenario: Brief a 4-aircraft formation for a dawn raid on an enemy airfield that has both fixed-wing and helicopter assets. Intelligence shows 2 SAM sites defending the base.
scenarios.context: Pre-planned strike mission. Airfield has hardened shelters and dispersed parking. Time on target is 0530 hours. Weather forecast is clear.
constraints: One aircraft has reduced weapons load

scenarios.scenario: Your altimeter setting is in hectopascals but the approach plate shows altitude in feet with QNH in inches of mercury. Convert and set the correct pressure.
scenarios.context: International flight arriving at a foreign military base. Night approach with published minima of 300 feet AGL.

scenarios.scenario: While landing in a crosswind of 25 knots gusting to 35, your aircraft touches down off-center on the runway. The aircraft begins to drift towards the runway edge.
scenarios.context: Wet runway surface. Fighter aircraft with narrow track landing gear. No arresting barrier available. Wind from the left.
constraints: Following aircraft is on short final
